Use case: ui-mockup. EDIT the supplied image in place. It is the edit target. Preserve its distinctive visual style, materials, colors, geometry, screen proportions, module silhouettes, readable English typography and UI chrome. Make a careful DATA ACCURACY PASS only, not a redesign.
The real sample has only these core source files: CheckoutController.cs (ApplyCoupon, Read, Estimate), CouponRules.cs (CalculateTotal, IsValid, DiscountPercent), CartState.cs (SetTotal and cart state). Any file tree should list just these three files and an Assets folder, no fabricated controllers/services/models hierarchy. Replace incorrect file captions or simply use role labels.
The source excerpt pane should show exactly these two readable lines, with NO invented line numbers:
cart.SetTotal(pricing.CalculateTotal(cart.Subtotal));
return view.Read(cart);
Label it "Source excerpt". If two source panes exist use this SAME excerpt in both. ApplyCoupon returns double, CalculateTotal returns double, Estimate returns double, Read returns double, IsValid returns bool, SetTotal returns void, DiscountPercent is a const double. Simpler role names without data types are fine.
The diagram has exactly SEVEN unique bodies and SIX directed source relations: ApplyCoupon -> IsValid, ApplyCoupon -> CalculateTotal, ApplyCoupon -> SetTotal, ApplyCoupon -> Read, Estimate -> CalculateTotal, CalculateTotal -> DiscountPercent. The first five are calls. The last is references. Arrowheads only at TARGET end. No duplicate body, extra relationship, reverse arrowhead, or execution sequence.
Keep "Pricing is shared by ApplyCoupon and Estimate." and Beginner / Expert controls. Cart preview is "Cart total (example)" with "120 → 96", "20% discount"; remove invented per-item prices, quantities or names from this preview, a small mug image may stay as an illustration. DiscountPercent role is "Pricing constant" (20), not mutable cart state. Preserve the theme selector and navigation, and footer "DESIGN STUDY · Static source relationships".
CRITICAL CABLE ROUTING: CalculateTotal currently appears to CALL SetTotal and Read; that is wrong. Reroute the third and fourth cables from ApplyCoupon all the way to SetTotal and Read, going around the central pricing cartridge without plugging into it. CalculateTotal should receive exactly TWO incoming call cables: from ApplyCoupon's second socket and from Estimate. DiscountPercent dashed reference cable MUST point upward FROM CalculateTotal INTO DiscountPercent, not downward. Remove any cable that ends on CalculateTotal from ApplyCoupon's third or fourth sockets. Keep the handsome graphite board / metallic tactile style, seven bodies, amber selected pricing cable.
